question: Re-fetch E 12026's descriptive/material/dating fields: does this catalogue still describe pleated linen before the New Kingdom, and what does it not supply about cut, pleating reconstruction or a universal wearing law? Label field transcriptions, not continuous prose.
source_locator: Louvre collections record E 12026 ; IF 10-14, "tunique" (Département des Antiquités égyptiennes), field values as returned live 2026-10-17T18:50Z: Description/Features "manches et corps plissés" with "Décor : sans décor"; Dimensions "Hauteur : 121 cm ; Largeur : 57 cm"; Materials and techniques "Matériau : lin" / "Technique : toile"; Places and dates "Date fin XIe dynastie ; début XIIe dynastie (contexte de fouilles) (-2045 - -1856)", "Date of discovery entre le 27 février et fin mai 1903", "Place of discovery tombe 13 (Assiout->Moyenne Égypte->Égypte)"; history: Chassinat/Palanque excavation, partage après fouilles, arrival 1903; current location "non exposé"; footer "Last updated on 28.03.2026" with caveat "The contents of this entry do not necessarily take account of the latest data." Field values confirmed identically in the raw downloaded HTML (worker scratch louvre-e12026.html lines 49, 478, 572, 593, 604, 612 and JSON-LD line 936).

retrieval_method: Live FetchURL of the exact named ARK URL (HTML text extraction), 2026-10-17 18:50Z; bracketed labels mark verbatim field transcriptions, not continuous prose; French field values retained as returned. Parallel curl GET of the same URL first timed out at 45 s (0 bytes), then returned HTTP 200, 11,781 bytes in ~53 s with HTTP/1.1; raw response kept only at reports/supplement-opencode-1/scratch/round7-09-source-scout/louvre-e12026.html (git-ignored). Fresh live call this round; no round-6 text copied.
basis: The record still describes pleated linen dated before the New Kingdom: "Matériau : lin" + "Technique : toile" (plain weave) with "manches et corps plissés", catalogued "fin XIe dynastie ; début XIIe dynastie (contexte de fouilles) (-2045 - -1856)" from excavation context tombe 13, Assiout. Every descriptive/material/date element the question names was retrieved this pass from the live record, so the object-level check that pleating is not an exclusively New Kingdom marker remains grounded in the catalogue's own current fields. The question's negative half is verified by absence in the same record: it supplies no cutting pattern or garment-construction data, no pleat-set/pleating-technique reconstruction, and no rule about who may wear what — Technique stops at "toile", Décor at "sans décor", and no wearing-law or status text appears in any retrieved field. Bibliography rows (Janssen 2020 p. 7, Jones 2014, Vogelsang-Eastwood 1993 pl. 30, Hall/Pedrini 1984, Chassinat & Palanque 1911 p. 163 pl. XXXIII, etc.) are bibliographic, not content, and none was counted as the passage.
limits: The dating is the museum's own catalogue attribution flagged "contexte de fouilles" — this audit neither re-dates the tomb group nor treats -2045/-1856 as independently verified; the record carries the museum caveat that its contents do not necessarily take account of the latest data (footer, last updated 28.03.2026), which is preserved rather than resolved. Nothing in the record licenses cut reconstruction, a pleating-technique reconstruction, or any universal wearing law, and none is inferred here; whether the tunic was everyday wear, display wear, or funerary equipment is not stated by the record. Artistic convention (how reliefs render pleats) is outside this object record and untested. A related-image carousel fragment displays a different span "-2045 / -1680 (Moyen…"; it was ambiguous in the returned text and was not used. Record fields are French; bracketed English labels and any translations are this worker's. Bibliography rows were not re-inspected beyond their listing.
